facts.content: Patient presents with a 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately 5 to 6 times per day.
Patient initially had two episodes of vomiting, which have now resolved.
Patient reports feeling dehydrated.
Patient reports decreased oral intake and appetite.
Patient reports weakness.
Patient denies abdominal pain.
Patient denies blood in stool.
Patient reports no current fever.
Patient denies headache or myalgia.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a blue inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension.
Patient's father died from bowel cancer.
Patient's mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and works as a software engineer.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient drinks alcohol socially.
No vital signs or examination findings are provided.
Diagnosed with acute gastroenteritis characterized by 3 days of watery diarrhea and mild dehydration without red-flag features.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis – 3 days watery diarrhea, mild dehydration, no red-flag features

facts.content: Asthma is assessed as stable with intermittent as-needed inhaler use.
facts.source_text: 2. Asthma – stable, intermittent PRN inhaler use

facts.content: Oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte is recommended.
Patient is encouraged to increase oral fluid intake.
Paracetamol is advised as needed for fever or aches.
Patient is advised to stay off work until at least 24 to 48 hours after being free of diarrhea.
Patient is instructed to return if diarrhea lasts more than 5 days, blood appears in stool, fever persists, or symptoms worsen.
facts.source_text: Return if diarrhea >5 d, blood in stool, persistent fever, worsening symptoms

facts.content: Follow-up is advised next week if there is no improvement.
